title: POC weekly - Redwood Private VPC pilot sync
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Focus on remaining networking issues (peering, route tables, NAT timeouts), planned kernel/runtime upgrade next week, KMS integration questions, and final run of latency/cost benchmarks. Agreed next steps: share peering diagram, schedule upgrade window, security to review KMS policy, Redwood to run end-to-end bench after changes.
topics: KMS/encryption key policy for private deployment
Benchmark results and tuning (batching, KV cache)
next_steps: Redwood: send updated network diagram and route table notes (Alex) - due 2026-07-17
Customer: confirm maintenance window for upgrade (Liam) - due 2026-07-20
Redwood SE: share benchmark spreadsheet + config used (Samir) - due 2026-07-18
Customer security: send KMS key policy snippet (Priya) - due 2026-07-19
All: follow-up sync after upgrade and bench run - schedule for week of 2026-07-20

Alex Chen - Send route table diag + notes about static routes and NAT timeout workaround by 2026-07-17
Samir Patel - Prepare runtime upgrade checklist and rollback playbook by 2026-07-16

attachments_references: Note: shared screen - network diagram (see attachment)
transcript: Meeting header: 2026-07-15 09:30 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya, Liam, Priya (Beacon)
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — networking updates, upgrade plan, bench results and action items. Maya you said there were a couple of new observations this week?

[00:28] Maya Gonzalez: yeah, hi, morning. so we still see intermittent 503s when we hit the private endpoint from our staging cluster. looks like route table changes correlate, so we suspect the peering route is flapping when the NAT scales up? not 100% sure.

[00:50] Liam O'Connor: to add, the NAT gateway logs show brief connection resets around 2:30am UTC when some autoscale events happen. might be a transient route propagation in our cloud provider, or the peering config isn't sticky across AZs.

[01:12] Samir Patel: ok, thanks — that tracks with a couple of things we saw in the runtime logs: there are short spikes of TLS handshake timeouts, which the client interprets as 502/503. one workaround is to add retry with jitter on the client side but we prefer fixing at infra level. did you share your route table exports?

[01:34] Maya Gonzalez: i shared a partial export last week; i'll push the full peering and route table tonight. apologies if there were missing routes earlier, i think the automation script skipped the cross-account route for az-b.

[01:56] Alex Chen: no worries, please share. Also Samir, on the runtime side we pushed a small patch last week to improve connection pooling and to keep the KV cache warm during short blips — might reduce observed errors. Are you on the latest runtime?

[02:18] Samir Patel: yes on our side we tested the patch in local env. the patch reduces cold-start overhead for new connections, but it doesn't fix underlying route flaps. If the peering is not stable we'll still see some failed requests during propagation.

[02:40] Priya Shah: quick security note — before we do any peering changes we need to confirm KMS policies and ensure keys are only accessible to the private control plane. can you confirm how Redwood's Private deployment integrates with customer KMS?

[03:02] Alex Chen: good question. for the pilot we support customer-managed KMS. Samir can explain the auth flow — it's mTLS to the control plane and the control plane requests keys from KMS using the IAM role you provision. we can send the KMS policy template after the call.

[03:26] Samir Patel: yeah, basically the control plane assumes your role and uses KMS Encrypt/Decrypt; we don't persist plaintext keys. But one caveat: if you're using an HSM-backed key, the latency for signing may increase a few ms per operation — usually negligible but worth noting for high-qps workloads.
[03:50] Liam O'Connor: understood. for our payment flows any small latency matters but more critical is reliability. If the HSM adds ms, it's ok as long as it's stable and predictable.
[04:12] Alex Chen: noted. we'll include HSM latency numbers in the benchmark sheet. speaking of benchmarks — Samir, can you run a fresh end-to-end bench once Maya shares the full route table?

[04:30] Samir Patel: yes, plan is to run bench with two configs: with KV cache primed and without, and with batching settings of 8/16. i'll include token/sec and p50/p95 latency plus cost estimates. expect results in the spreadsheet.
[04:54] Maya Gonzalez: also we had question about rollout — when you do the runtime/kernel upgrade, how do you handle canary vs full rollout? if something goes wrong can we rollback quickly?

[05:16] Alex Chen: we do staged canary by default. Samir will do a 10% canary across two AZs, monitor p95 and error rate, then ramp. rollback is automated — about a 5-minscaler to flip routes back if threshold exceeded. we'll share the rollback playbook.

[05:40] Samir Patel: to add, we keep the previous model variant pinned for 30 minutes after a rollout so traffic can fall back automatically. also we have tracing hooks to compare outputs during canary to detect regressions.
[06:02] Liam O'Connor: good. what's the planned upgrade window? we prefer late-night to minimize payment traffic impact. next week works for us if we get the prep checklist.
[06:24] Alex Chen: tentative plan is Wed 2026-07-22 01:00–02:30 UTC. we'll treat that as a provisional slot until you confirm. Samir will prepare the checklist and runbook before then.
[06:46] Maya Gonzalez: sounds fine. Priya, any security blockers to that schedule?

[06:58] Priya Shah: main blocker is KMS verification and audit log access. we need to validate audit trails and ensure Redwood's control plane role is adequately scoped. i can review once you send the policy template.

[07:18] Alex Chen: we'll send the template. Also quick note on routing — we recommend static routes for the control plane prefix to avoid propagation issues during scale events. Maya, can your infra team do a static route test in staging?
[07:40] Maya Gonzalez: yes we can. i'll run a staging test to enforce static routes and see if NAT scaling still causes resets. i'll capture tcpdump and route logs for the bench.

[08:02] Samir Patel: perfect. for the bench we also want to test two model quantization profiles — one higher quality + bigger memory and one quantized to lower memory. the idea is to surface CPU/GPU/latency tradeoffs in your private deployment.
[08:28] Liam O'Connor: one practical question — when you say private control plane, is telemetry still sent to Redwood? we need to know what telemetry leaves the VPC for compliance.

[08:46] Alex Chen: telemetry is optional. for Private we can disable telemetry and only send minimal heartbeat + encrypted usage metrics, or in fully air-gapped setups none leaves. we'll document what fields are collected and give you toggles.
[09:06] Priya Shah: we'll need the exact list of telemetry fields for SOC2 review. especially anything that might contain PII or customer data.
[09:22] Alex Chen: absolutely — we'll add that to the security packet. Samir, can you confirm which logs include request/response metadata and which are scrubbed?

[09:36] Samir Patel: we mask PII by default in request logs and we never store full user content unless you opt-in for evals. the control plane keeps error traces and token-level cost metrics. i'll attach the logs schema.
[09:56] Maya Gonzalez: thanks. small note — earlier in our POC we saw a spike in token cost when batching spiked unexpectedly. any guidance on safe batching thresholds?

[10:16] Samir Patel: generally, batching helps cost but can add to p95 latency. for your payment flows i'd recommend conservative batching (4–8) and KV cache enabled. our optimize tool will suggest the sweet spot after we analyze the traces.
[10:40] Liam O'Connor: is there a way to pin certain routes to prefer lower-latency AZs? we want to ensure traffic to the primary region sticks to the fastest path.
[10:56] Alex Chen: yes you can set routing policies — we support region preference and fallback. we'll include sample route policies in the network guide we send.
[11:14] Maya Gonzalez: ok i'll run the static route test and share results. on KMS i'll loop in Priya and we should have the policy by Friday.
[11:30] Priya Shah: that'll be tight but doable, i'll aim for 2026-07-19 as discussed.

[11:44] Samir Patel: about the kernel/runtime upgrade — small detail: the upgrade includes a new attention kernel that reduces memory transient by ~12% for the models we tested. that helps with model variant density on a single GPU.
[12:06] Liam O'Connor: nice. any risk of incompat with older model formats?

[12:16] Samir Patel: no breaking changes; we run a compatibility suite. the only caveat is some custom ops in previous internal builds; we didn't see those in your models, but worth double-checking the model artifact.
[12:36] Maya Gonzalez: we do have a custom tokenizer patch in our pipeline, could that be an issue?
[12:44] Samir Patel: if the tokenizer output conforms to expected token ids it's fine; if there's custom token merging then we might need a small adapter. please share a sample artifact.

[13:02] Alex Chen: note for next steps — Samir will run bench once Maya shares full route tables and model sample; Alex will send network and security docs; Priya will send KMS policy; Liam will confirm maintenance window.
[13:20] Maya Gonzalez: one more question — do you keep audit logs in customer S3 or Redwood-managed?

[13:32] Alex Chen: for Private deployments we can either push logs to your S3 or store locally in the private control plane with optional S3 export. most enterprise customers want S3 so they control retention.
[13:52] Priya Shah: S3 export is preferred. also will you support SAML/SSO integration for the console?
[14:04] Alex Chen: yes SAML SSO supported; we'll provide setup docs and metadata. for pilot we can do a test integration in staging.
[14:22] Liam O'Connor: perfect. any blockers from Redwood's side to schedule the upgrade next week?
[14:34] Samir Patel: just the checklist — i'll finalize it by Friday and post it to the repo with rollback steps. we'll also run a small dry-run in our QA before touching production.
[14:52] Maya Gonzalez: sounds good. i'll coordinate with infra for static routes and send logs. Also we'll collect tcpdump around the time of scaling so you can see packet-level behavior.
[15:08] Alex Chen: awesome. i'll follow up with the network diag and the control plane KMS template. any other questions?
[15:20] Priya Shah: nothing else from security for now, thanks.
[15:30] Liam O'Connor: no further questions, thanks everyone.

[15:36] Alex Chen: recap of agreed action items and owners — (1) Maya share full peering & route tables (2) Alex send network + security docs (3) Samir run bench and share spreadsheet (4) Priya provide KMS policy (5) Liam confirm maintenance window. we'll aim for follow up sync after the upgrade and bench run. thanks all.
[15:58] End of meeting
